returned with Duke Lì and established him.
In the autumn, the ninth month, on the day dìnghài,
Duke Zhāo fled to Wèi.
On the day jǐhài,
Duke Lì was established.
A2.12 *The Annals of the Twelfth Year of Duke Huán*
A2.12.1 In the spring of the twelfth year, the first month.
A2.12.2 In the summer, the sixth month, on the day rényín,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qǐ
and the Viscount of Jǔ to form a covenant at Qǔchí.
A2.12.3 In the autumn, the seventh month, on the day dìnghài,
the Duke met with the Duke of Sòng
and the people of Yàn to form a covenant at Gǔqiū.
A2.12.4 In the eighth month, on the day rénchén,
Yuè, the Marquis of Chén, died.
A2.12.5 The Duke met with the Duke of Sòng at Xū.
A2.12.6 In the winter, the eleventh month,
the Duke met with the Duke of Sòng at Guī.
A2.12.7 On the day bǐngxū,
the Duke met with the Earl of Zhèng
and formed a covenant at Wǔfù.
A2.12.8 On the day bǐngxū,
Jìn, the Marquis of Wèi, died.
A2.12.9 In the twelfth month,
he attacked Sòng with the Zhèng army.
On the day dīngwèi,
they fought in Sòng.
B2.12 *The Commentary on the Twelfth Year of Duke Huán*
B2.12.1 In the summer of the twelfth year,
the covenant at Qǔchí
was to bring peace between Qǐ
and Jǔ.
B2.12.2 The Duke wished to bring peace between Sòng and Zhèng.
In the autumn,
the Duke and the Duke of Sòng formed a covenant at the hill of Gòudú.
Since the completion of peace with Sòng could not yet be known,
they met again at Xū;
in the winter,
they met again at Guī.
The Duke of Sòng declined the peace;
therefore, the Duke formed a covenant with the Earl of Zhèng at Wǔfù,
then led an army to attack Sòng
and fought there
because Sòng was untrustworthy.
The gentleman says:
“If trustworthiness is not maintained,
a covenant is of no benefit.
The *Odes* says:
‘The gentleman repeatedly forms covenants,
and disorder thereby grows.’
This refers to a lack of trustworthiness.”
B2.12.3 Chǔ attacked Jiǎo
and encamped at its southern gate.
The Mò'áo Qū Xiá said:
“Jiǎo is small and impulsive;
being impulsive, it lacks planning.
I request that we do not obstruct the wood-gatherers, in order to lure them out.”
This was followed.
The people of Jiǎo captured thirty people.
The next day,
the people of Jiǎo vied to come out
and chased the Chǔ laborers into the mountains.
The Chǔ army occupied their northern gate
and set an ambush at the foot of the mountains.
They defeated them soundly.
They made a covenant under the city walls and returned.
B2.12.4 In the campaign to attack Jiǎo,
the Chǔ army divided to cross at Péng.
The people of Luó wished to attack them.
They sent Bó Jiā to spy on them.
He went three times and counted them.
A2.13 *The Annals of the Thirteenth Year of Duke Huán*
A2.13.1 In the spring of the thirteenth year, the second month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Jì
and the Earl of Zhèng.
On the day jǐsì,
they fought against the Marquis of Qí,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
and the people of Yàn.
The army of Qí,
the army of Sòng,
the army of Wèi,
and the army of Yàn were utterly defeated.
A2.13.2 In the third month,
Duke Xuān of Wèi was buried.
A2.13.3 In the summer,
there was a great flood.
A2.13.4 In the autumn, the seventh month.
A2.13.5 In the winter, the tenth month.
B2.13 *The Commentary on the Thirteenth Year of Duke Huán*
B2.13.1 In the thirteenth year, in spring,
Qū Xiá of Chǔ attacked Luó,
and Dòu Bóbǐ saw him off.
Upon returning,
he said to his driver:
“The Mòáo is certain to be defeated.
He lifts his feet high;
his mind is not firm.”
He then went to see the Viscount of Chǔ
and said:
“You must send reinforcements!”
The Viscount of Chǔ declined.
He went inside and told his wife, Dèng Màn.
Dèng Màn said:
“The Grand Officer was likely not speaking of the size of the multitude,
but rather suggesting that you, my Lord, should soothe the common people with good faith,
instruct the various officials with virtue,
and overawe the Mòáo with the threat of punishment.
The Mòáo has grown accustomed to the campaign at Pú Sāo
and will act willfully;
he will certainly slight the state of Luó.
If you, my Lord, do not steady and soothe the troops,
will he not fail to make preparations?
What he meant was for you, my Lord, to instruct the multitude
and be diligent in steadying and soothing them,
to summon the various officials
and encourage them with excellent virtue,
and to see the Mòáo
and inform him that Heaven does not grant its favor easily.
Otherwise,
how could he not know that the Chǔ forces have already been fully deployed?”
The Viscount of Chǔ sent a man of Lài to pursue him,
but he could not catch up.
The Mòáo had it proclaimed throughout the army:
“Those who offer remonstrance shall be punished!”
When they reached Yān,
they crossed the river in a disordered line,
and subsequently remained without order.
Moreover, they made no preparations.
When they reached Luó,
Luó and the Lú Róng attacked from both sides
and heavily defeated them.
The Mòáo hanged himself in Huāng Gǔ.
The other commanders were imprisoned at Yě Fù
to await punishment.
The Viscount of Chǔ said:
“It is my fault.”
He pardoned them all.
B2.13.2 Sòng repeatedly demanded bribes from Zhèng.
Zhèng could not bear the orders;
therefore, together with Jì,
Lǔ, and Qí, they
fought Sòng, Wèi, and Yàn.
The location of the battle is not recorded
because it took place late.
B2.13.3 The people of Zhèng came to request the renewal of friendly relations.
A2.14 The Annals of the Fourteenth Year of Duke Huán
A2.14.1 In the fourteenth year, in spring, the first month,
the Duke met the Earl of Zhèng at Cáo.
A2.14.2 There was no ice.
A2.14.3 In summer, the fifth month,
the Earl of Zhèng sent his younger brother Yǔ to come and make a covenant.
A2.14.4 In autumn, the eighth month, on the day Rénshēn,
the Imperial Granary suffered a fire.
A2.14.5 On the day Yǐhài,
the Cháng sacrifice was performed.
A2.14.6 In winter, the twelfth month, on the day Dīngsì,
Lùfù, the Marquis of Qí, died.
A2.14.7 The people of Sòng, along with the people of Qí,
the people of Cài,
the people of Wèi,
and the people of Chén, attacked Zhèng.
B2.14 The Commentary on the Fourteenth Year of Duke Huán
B2.14.1 In the fourteenth year, in spring,
there was a meeting at Cáo.
The people of Cáo presented ritual provisions;
this was in accordance with ritual propriety.
B2.14.2 In summer,
Zǐrén of Zhèng came to seek a covenant
and to cultivate the relations established at the meeting in Cáo.
B2.14.3 In autumn, the eighth month, on the day Rénshēn,
the Imperial Granary suffered a fire.
On the day Yǐhài,
the Cháng sacrifice was performed.
This was recorded
because it did not cause harm.
B2.14.4 In winter,
the people of Sòng, together with the feudal lords, attacked Zhèng,
to retaliate for the battle of Sòng.
They burned the Qú Mén gate.
They entered
and reached the Dà Kuí road.
They attacked the eastern suburbs
and took Niú Shǒu.
They returned with the rafters of the Great Temple
to serve as rafters for the Lú Mén gate.
A2.15 The Annals of the Fifteenth Year of Duke Huán
A2.15.1 In the fifteenth year, in spring, the second month,
the Heavenly King sent Jiā Fǔ to come and request carriages.
A2.15.2 In the third month, on the day Yǐwèi,
the Heavenly King passed away.
A2.15.3 In summer, the fourth month, on the day Jǐsì,
Duke Xī of Qí was buried.
A2.15.4 In the fifth month,
Tū, the Earl of Zhèng, fled and escaped to Cài.
A2.15.5 Hū, the Heir Apparent of Zhèng, returned again to Zhèng.
A2.15.6 Xǔ Shū entered Xǔ.
A2.15.7 The Duke met the Marquis of Qí at Ài.
A2.15.8 The people of Zhù,
the people of Mǒu,
and the people of Gé came to pay court.
A2.15.9 In autumn, the ninth month,
Tū, the Earl of Zhèng, entered Lì.
A2.15.10 In winter, the eleventh month,
the Duke met the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
and the Marquis of Chén at Tuó
to attack Zhèng.
B2.15 The Commentary on the Fifteenth Year of Duke Huán
B2.15.1 In the fifteenth year, in spring,
the Heavenly King sent Jiā Fǔ to come and request carriages;
this was contrary to ritual propriety.
The feudal lords do not offer carriages
or robes as tribute,
and the Son of Heaven does not privately request wealth.
B2.15.2 Zhài Zhòng monopolized power,
and the Earl of Zhèng was distressed by this;
he sent his son-in-law Yōng Jiǔ to kill him.
He intended to feast him in the suburbs.
Yōng Jī knew of this
and said to her mother:
“Who is closer, a father or a husband?”
Her mother said:
“Any man can be one’s husband,
but one has only one father;
how can they be compared?”
Consequently, she told Zhài Zhòng:
“The Yōng family has left their home
and intends to feast you in the suburbs;
I find this suspicious,
so I am telling you.”
Zhài Zhòng killed Yōng Jiǔ
and exposed his corpse by the pond of the Zhōu family.
Duke Lì loaded the body into his carriage to depart,
saying:
“When one discusses a plot with a woman,
it is only right that he should die.”
In summer,
Duke Lì fled and escaped to Cài.
B2.15.3 In the sixth month, on the day Yǐhài,
Duke Zhāo entered Zhèng.
B2.15.4 Xǔ Shū entered Xǔ.
B2.15.5 The Duke met the Marquis of Qí at Ài,
to plan for the settlement of Xǔ.
B2.15.6 In autumn,
the Earl of Zhèng, acting through the people of Lì, killed Tán Bó,
and subsequently resided in Lì.
B2.15.7 In winter,
they met at Tuó
to plan an attack on Zhèng,
intending to reinstate Duke Lì.
They did not succeed and returned.
A2.16 The Annals of the Sixteenth Year of Duke Huán
A2.16.1 In the sixteenth year, in spring, the first month,
the Duke met the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Cài,
and the Marquis of Wèi at Cáo.
A2.16.2 In summer, the fourth month,
the Duke met the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
the Marquis of Chén,
and the Marquis of Cài to attack Zhèng.
A2.16.3 In autumn, the seventh month,
the Duke arrived from attacking Zhèng.
In the winter,
fortified Xiàng.
In the eleventh month,
the Marquis of Wèi, Shuò, fled to Qí.
*The Commentary on the Sixteenth Year of Duke Huán*
In the spring of the sixteenth year, the first month,
a meeting was held at Cáo
to plan an attack on Zhèng.
In the summer,
Zhèng was attacked.
In the autumn, the seventh month,
the Duke arrived from the attack on Zhèng,
performing the ritual of drinking upon arrival.
In the winter,
Xiàng was fortified.
This was recorded
because it was done at the proper season.
Previously,
Duke Xuān of Wèi had an incestuous affair with Yí Jiāng,
who gave birth to Jí Zǐ,
who was entrusted to the Noble Scion of the Right.
A wife was sought for him from Qí,
but as she was beautiful,
the Duke took her for himself.
She gave birth to Shòu and Shuò.
Shòu was entrusted to the Noble Scion of the Left.
Yí Jiāng hanged herself.
Xuān Jiāng and the Noble Scion Shuò conspired against Jí Zǐ.
The Duke sent him to Qí.
He also sent bandits to wait for him at Shēn,
intending to kill him.
Prince Shòu told him
and urged him to flee.
He refused,
saying:
"If I disregard my father's command,
of what use am I as a son?
If there were a state without a father,
then it would be permissible."
When it came time to depart,
Shòu made him drink wine.
Prince Shòu then carried the signal flag and went ahead;
the bandits killed him.
When Jí Zǐ arrived,
he said:
"I am the one you seek.
What crime did he commit?
Please kill me!"
They killed him as well.
The two Noble Scions consequently resented Duke Huì.
In the eleventh month,
the Noble Scion of the Left, Xiè,
and the Noble Scion of the Right, Zhí, established Gōngzǐ Qiánmóu.
Duke Huì fled to Qí.
*The Annals of the Seventeenth Year of Duke Huán*
In the seventeenth year, spring, the first month, on the day Bǐngchén,
the Duke met the Marquis of Qí
and the Marquis of Jǐ for a covenant at Huáng.
In the second month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Duke met Yífù of Zhū
and made a covenant at Cuǐ.
In the fifth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
they fought with the army of Qí at Xī.
In the sixth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
the Marquis of Cài, Fēngrén, died.
In the autumn, the eighth month,
Cài Jì returned from Chén to Cài.
On the day Guǐsì,
Marquis Huán of Cài was buried.
Along with the people of Sòng
and the people of Wèi, they attacked Zhū.
In the winter, on the first day of the tenth month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
*The Commentary on the Seventeenth Year of Duke Huán*
In the spring of the seventeenth year,
they made a covenant at Huáng
to bring peace between Qí
and Jǐ,
and also to plan for the affairs of Wèi.
The covenant with Yífù of Zhū at Cuǐ
was to renew the covenant of Miè.
In the summer,
the battle with the army of Qí at Xī
was over border matters.
At that time, the people of Qí encroached upon the borders of Lǔ,
and the border officials came to report it.
The Duke said:
"In matters of the borders,
be cautious in guarding your post
and prepare for the unexpected;
just do your utmost in preparation.
When the matter arrives, we fight;
why else would you report?"
Marquis Huán of Cài died.
The people of Cài summoned Cài Jì from Chén.
In the autumn,
Cài Jì returned from Chén to Cài;
the people of Cài praised him.
The attack on Zhū
was the intent of Sòng.
In the winter, on the first day of the tenth month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
The day was not recorded
because the official failed to do so.
The Son of Heaven has solar officials,
and the feudal lords have solar attendants.
The solar official holds the rank of a high minister to determine the days;
this is the ritual.
The solar attendants do not lose track of the days,
so as to present them to the various officials at court.
Previously,
the Earl of Zhèng intended to make Gāo Qúmí a high minister.
Duke Zhāo disliked him
and firmly remonstrated,
but was not listened to.
When Duke Zhāo acceded to the throne,
Gāo Qúmí feared that the Duke would kill him.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
he assassinated Duke Zhāo
and established Gōngzǐ Wěi.
The superior man said,
"Duke Zhāo knew whom to dislike."
Gōngzǐ Dá said:
"Will Lord Gāo be executed?
His accumulation of malice is extreme."
*The Annals of the Eighteenth Year of Duke Huán*
In the eighteenth year, the spring of the royal first month,
the Duke met the Marquis of Qí at Luò.
The Duke and his wife Jiāng Shì then went to Qí.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Duke passed away in Qí.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the Duke's funeral procession arrived from Qí.
In the autumn, the seventh month.
In the winter, the twelfth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
our ruler, Duke Huán, was buried.
*The Commentary on the Eighteenth Year of Duke Huán*
In the spring of the eighteenth year,
the Duke was about to go on a journey,
and consequently went with Jiāng Shì to Qí.
Shēn Xú said:
"Women have their families,
and men have their chambers;
they should not behave profanely toward one another.
This is what is called being ritual.
To change this
will surely lead to ruin."
The Duke met the Marquis of Qí at Luò,
and then accompanied Wén Jiāng to Qí.
The Marquis of Qí had an illicit affair with her.
The Duke rebuked her.
She reported this to the Marquis.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Marquis feasted the Duke.
He sent Gōngzǐ Péngshēng to assist the Duke into his carriage,
and the Duke passed away in the carriage.
The people of Lǔ reported to Qí, saying:
"Our meager ruler feared your might,
and not daring to remain at ease,
he came to renew our old friendship.
The rituals were completed but he did not return.
There is no one to whom we can attribute the fault,
and it looks bad to the feudal lords.
We request that Péngshēng be used to remove the blame."
The people of Qí killed Péngshēng.
In the autumn,
the Marquis of Qí encamped at Shǒuzhǐ;
Zǐ Wěi met him there,
and Gāo Qúmí assisted him.
In the seventh month, on the day Wùxū,
the people of Qí killed Zǐ Wěi
and tore Gāo Qúmí apart between chariots.
Zhài Zhòng met Zhèng Zǐ in Chén
and installed him.
On this journey,
Zhài Zhòng knew of the plot,
so he claimed illness and did not go.
People said:
“Zhài Zhòng avoided trouble through wisdom.”
Zhòng said:
“Truly so.”
B2.18.3 Zhōu Gōng desired to assassinate Zhuāng Wáng
and install Wángzǐ Kè.
Xīnbó informed the King,
and then with the King killed Zhōu Gōng Hēijiān.
Wángzǐ Kè fled to Yān.
Initially,
Zǐyí was favored by Huán Wáng,
and Huán Wáng entrusted him to Zhōu Gōng.
Xīnbó remonstrated, saying:
“Having a consort equal to the queen, a concubine's son equal to the legitimate heir, two centers of government, and rival cities
are the roots of disorder.”
Zhōu Gōng did not follow this,
thus he met his end.
A3.1 The Annals of the First Year of Zhuāng Gōng
A3.1.1 In the spring of the first year,
the Royal first month.
A3.1.2 In the third month,
the lady went into exile in Qí.
A3.1.3 In summer,
Shànbó escorted Wáng Jī.
A3.1.4 In autumn,
a lodge for Wáng Jī was built outside.
A3.1.5 In winter, the tenth month, on the day Yǐhài,
Chén Hóu Lín died.
A3.1.6 The King sent Róng Shū to come and confer the mandate on Huán Gōng.
Wáng Jī went to her home in Qí.
A3.1.8 The army of Qí relocated [the people of] Jǐpíng,
Zī, and Wú.
B3.1 The Commentary for the First Year of Zhuāng Gōng
B3.1.1 In the spring of the first year,
ascending the throne is not mentioned,
because Wén Jiāng had gone out.
B3.1.2 In the third month,
the lady went into exile in Qí.
She is not called of the Jiāng clan,
because it signifies the severing of kinship,
which is in accordance with ritual.
B3.1.3 In autumn,
a lodge for Wáng Jī was built outside.
Building it outside
was in accordance with ritual.
A3.2 The Annals of the Second Year of Zhuāng Gōng
A3.2.1 In the spring of the second year,
the Royal second month,
Chén Zhuāng Gōng was buried.
A3.2.2 In summer,
Gōngzǐ Qìngfù led an army to attack Yúqiū.
A3.2.3 In autumn, the seventh month,
Wáng Jī of Qí died.
A3.2.4 In winter, the twelfth month,
the lady of the Jiāng clan met with the Qí Hóu at Zhuó.
A3.2.5 On the day Yǐyǒu,
Sòng Gōng Féng died.
B3.2 The Commentary for the Second Year of Zhuāng Gōng
B3.2.1 In the winter of the second year,
the lady of the Jiāng clan met with the Qí Hóu at Zhuó.
This was recorded
as an illicit act.
A3.3 The Annals of the Third Year of Zhuāng Gōng
A3.3.1 In the spring of the third year,
the Royal first month,
Nì met with the army of Qí to attack Wèi.
A3.3.2 In summer, the fourth month,
Sòng Zhuāng Gōng was buried.
A3.3.3 In the fifth month,
Huán Wáng was buried.
A3.3.4 In autumn,
Jǐ Jì entered Qí with Xī.
A3.3.5 In winter,
the Duke halted at Huá.
B3.3 The Commentary for the Third Year of Zhuāng Gōng
B3.3.1 In the spring of the third year,
Nì met with the army of Qí to attack Wèi;
this shows displeasure with him.
B3.3.2 In summer, the fifth month,
Huán Wáng was buried;
it was late.
B3.3.3 In autumn,
Jǐ Jì entered Qí with Xī;
the state of Jǐ began to split then.
B3.3.4 In winter,
the Duke halted at Huá,
intending to meet with Zhèng Bó
to plan for Jǐ.
Zhèng Bó declined due to difficulties.
For all armies,
staying one night is called shè,
staying two nights is called xìn,
and exceeding xìn is called cì.
A3.4 The Annals of the Fourth Year of Zhuāng Gōng
A3.4.1 In the spring of the fourth year,
the Royal second month,
the lady of the Jiāng clan entertained the Qí Hóu at Zhùqiū.
A3.4.2 In the third month,
Jǐ Bójiāng died.
A3.4.3 In summer,
Qí Hóu,
Chén Hóu,
and Zhèng Bó met at Chuí.
A3.4.4 Jǐ Hóu finally left his state.
A3.4.5 In the sixth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
Qí Hóu buried Jǐ Bójiāng.
A3.4.6 In autumn, the seventh month.
A3.4.7 In winter,
the Duke and the men of Qí hunted at Zhuó.
B3.4 The Commentary for the Fourth Year of Zhuāng Gōng
B3.4.1 In the spring of the fourth year,
the Royal first month,
Chǔ Wǔ Wáng organized the jīngshī formation,
handed out single halberds to the army,
and used them to attack Suí.
About to practice abstinence,
he went in and told Lady Dèng Màn:
“My heart is fluttering.”
Dèng Màn sighed and said:
“The King’s blessings are exhausted.
To be full and then flutter
is the Way of Heaven.
The former lords must know this;
therefore, as he faced military affairs
and was about to issue a grand command,
they made the King’s heart flutter.
If the ranks of the army suffer no loss,
and the King dies on the march,
it is a blessing for the state.”
The King then set out
and died under a mán tree.
Lìngyǐn Dòuqí and Mòáo Qū Zhòng
cleared the road and bridged the Zhà River,
and arrayed the army facing Suí.
The people of Suí were afraid
and made peace.
Mòáo, with the King’s command, entered
to covenant with Suí Hóu,
and requested a meeting at the bank of the Hàn River,
and then returned.
Only after crossing the Hàn
did they announce the death.
B3.4.2 Jǐ Hóu could not humble himself before Qí,
so he gave his lands to Jǐ Jì.
In summer,
Jǐ Hóu finally left his state,
to avoid the troubles from Qí.
A3.5 The Annals of the Fifth Year of Zhuāng Gōng
A3.5.1 In the spring of the fifth year,
the Royal first month.
A3.5.2 In summer,
the lady of the Jiāng clan went to the army of Qí.
A3.5.3 In autumn,
Ní Lílái came for an audience.
A3.5.4 Winter,
the Gōng met with the Qí Rén,
Sòng Rén,
Chén Rén,
and Cài Rén to attack Wèi.
B3.5 *Zhuāng Gōng Wǔ Nián Zhuàn*
B3.5.1 In the autumn of the fifth year,
Ní Lí Lái came for an audience.
He is named
because he had not yet received the Wáng’s command.
B3.5.2 In winter,
they attacked Wèi,
to install Huì Gōng.
A3.6 *Zhuāng Gōng Liù Nián Jīng*
A3.6.1 In the spring of the sixth year,
in the Wáng’s first month,
the Wáng Rén Zǐ Tū rescued Wèi.
A3.6.2 In summer, the sixth month,
Wèi Hóu Shuò entered Wèi.
A3.6.3 In autumn,
the Gōng arrived from attacking Wèi.
A3.6.4 Míng locusts.
A3.6.5 In winter,
the Qí Rén came to return the captives of Wèi.
B3.6 *Zhuāng Gōng Liù Nián Zhuàn*
B3.6.1 In the spring of the sixth year,
the Wáng Rén rescued Wèi.
In summer,
the Wèi Hóu entered,
exiled Gōngzǐ Qiánmóu to Zhōu,
exiled Níng Guì to Qín,
killed the Zuǒ Gōngzǐ Xiè
and the Yòu Gōngzǐ Zhí,
and then ascended the throne.
The Jūnzǐ considered the two Gōngzǐ’s installation of Qiánmóu to be without measure.
For one who can secure the position
must take measure of the root and the branches,
and only then establish the center.
Not knowing the root,
they should not have planned;
knowing that the root had no branches,
they should not have been forceful.
The *Shī* says:
“The root and branches for a hundred generations.”
B3.6.2 In winter,
the Qí Rén came to return the treasures of Wèi,
as Wén Jiāng requested it.
B3.6.3 Chǔ Wén Wáng attacked Shēn.
He passed Dèng.
Dèng Qí Hóu said:
“He is my nephew.”
He stopped him and entertained him.
Zhuīshēng, Dānshēng, and Yǎngshēng
requested to kill the Chǔ Zǐ.
Dèng Hóu did not permit it.
The three nephews said:
“The one who will destroy the state of Dèng
must be this man.
If you do not plan early,
later the ruler will bite his navel.
Can it still be planned for then?
To plan for it,
now is the time.”
Dèng Hóu said:
“People will not eat my leftovers.”
They replied:
“If you do not follow your three ministers,
then the Shè Jì will truly not receive blood sacrifices,
and from where will the ruler take leftovers?”
He did not follow them.
The following year,
Chǔ Zǐ attacked Dèng.
In the sixteenth year,
Chǔ again attacked Dèng,
and destroyed it.
A3.7 *Zhuāng Gōng Qī Nián Jīng*
A3.7.1 In the spring of the seventh year,
the Fū Rén Jiāng Shì met the Qí Hóu at Fáng.
A3.7.2 In summer, the fourth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
at night, the fixed stars were not visible.
At midnight,
stars fell like rain.
A3.7.3 In autumn,
there were great floods.
A3.7.4 There was no wheat
or seedlings.
A3.7.5 In winter,
the Fū Rén Jiāng Shì met the Qí Hóu at Gǔ.
B3.7 *Zhuāng Gōng Qī Nián Zhuàn*
B3.7.1 In the spring of the seventh year,
Wén Jiāng met the Qí Hóu at Fáng,
which was the desire of Qí.
B3.7.2 In summer,
the fixed stars were not visible,
because the night was bright.
Stars fell like rain,
falling together with the rain.
B3.7.3 In autumn,
there was no wheat
or seedlings,
which did not harm the good grain.
A3.8 *Zhuāng Gōng Bā Nián Jīng*
A3.8.1 In the spring of the eighth year,
the Wáng’s first month,
the army halted at Láng
to wait for the Chén Rén
and Cài Rén.
A3.8.2 On the day Jiǎwǔ,
they reviewed the troops.
A3.8.3 In summer,
the army and the Qí army besieged Chéng.
Chéng surrendered to the Qí army.
A3.8.4 In autumn,
the army returned.
A3.8.5 In winter, the eleventh month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Qí Wúzhī murdered his ruler Zhū’ér.
B3.8 *Zhuāng Gōng Bā Nián Zhuàn*
B3.8.1 In the spring of the eighth year,
reviewing the troops at the temple
was in accordance with ritual.
B3.8.2 In summer,
the army and the Qí army besieged Chéng.
Chéng surrendered to the Qí army.
Zhòng Qìngfù requested to attack the Qí army.
The Gōng said:
“No.
It is actually that I lack virtue;
what crime has the Qí army committed?
The crime stems from me.
The *Xià Shū* says:
‘Gāoyáo diligently sowed virtue;
virtue [being sown],
then people submitted.’
For now let us strive to cultivate virtue
to wait for the right time!”
In autumn,
the army returned.
Because of this, the Jūnzǐ praised Zhuāng Gōng of Lǔ.
B3.8.3 The Qí Hóu sent Lián Chèn,
Guǎn Zhìfù to garrison Kuíqiū,
sending them when the melons were in season,
saying:
“When the melons come again, you will be replaced.”
When the term of service was up,
no message arrived from the Gōng.
They requested to be replaced,
but he did not permit it.
Therefore, they plotted to cause a rebellion.
Xī Gōng’s younger brother of the same mother was named Yí Zhòngnián,
who fathered Gōngsūn Wúzhī;
he was favored by Xī Gōng,
and his clothing and ritual status were like those of the legitimate heir.
Xiāng Gōng demoted him.
The two men relied on him to cause the rebellion.
Lián Chèn had a younger female cousin in the Gōng’s palace
who was not favored;
he sent her to spy on the Gōng.
He said:
“If successful,
I will make you the Fū Rén.”
In winter, the twelfth month,
the Qí Hóu traveled to Gūfén
and then went hunting at Bèiqiū.
He saw a large boar.
His attendants said:
“It is Gōngzǐ Péngshēng!”
The Gōng was angry
and said:
“Péngshēng dares to show himself!”
He shot it.
The boar stood up like a man and wailed.
The Gōng was terrified
and fell from the carriage,
injuring his foot
and losing his shoe.
Returning, he demanded his shoe from the attendant Fèi.
He could not find it,
so he whipped him,
drawing blood.
Fèi ran out
and met the rebels at the gate.
They seized and bound him.
Fèi said:
“How could I resist?”
He bared his back and showed it to them.
They believed him.
Fèi asked to enter first.
He hid the Duke and came out;
he fought
and died within the gate.
Shí Zhī Fēn Rú died at the foot of the steps.
Then they entered
and killed Mèng Yáng on the bed.
They said:
“This is not the ruler;
he does not look like him.”
They saw the Duke’s feet under the door
and so assassinated him,
then set up Wú Zhī.
Earlier,
when Duke Xiāng was established,
he was erratic.
Bào Shū Yá said:
“The ruler treats the people with contempt;
disorder is about to arise.”
He escorted Prince Xiǎo Bái and fled to Jǔ.
When disorder arose,
Guǎn Yí Wú and Shào Hū escorted Prince Jiū and fled to Lǔ.
B3.8.4 Initially,
Gōngsūn Wú Zhī was cruel to Yōng Lǐn.
A3.9 The Annals of Duke Zhuāng, Ninth Year
A3.9.1 In the spring of the ninth year,
the people of Qí killed Wú Zhī.
A3.9.2 The Duke and the Great Officers of Qí made a covenant at Jì.
A3.9.3 In summer,
the Duke attacked Qí
to escort Prince Jiū back.
Xiǎo Bái of Qí entered Qí.
A3.9.4 In autumn, in the seventh month on the day dīng yǒu,
Duke Xiāng of Qí was buried.
A3.9.5 In the eighth month on the day gēng shēn,
they fought the Qí army at Gān Shí,
and our army was soundly defeated.
A3.9.6 In the ninth month,
the people of Qí took Prince Jiū and killed him.
A3.9.7 In winter,
the Zhū River was dredged.
B3.9 The Commentary of Duke Zhuāng, Ninth Year
B3.9.1 In the spring of the ninth year,
Yōng Lǐn killed Wú Zhī.
B3.9.2 The Duke and the Great Officers of Qí made a covenant at Jì,
as Qí had no ruler.
B3.9.3 In summer,
the Duke attacked Qí
to escort Prince Jiū back.
Duke Huán entered first from Jǔ.
B3.9.4 In autumn,
the army fought the Qí army at Gān Shí,
and our army was soundly defeated.
The Duke lost his war chariot
and returned in a relay carriage.
Qín Zǐ and Liáng Zǐ, using the Duke’s flag
to withdraw by a lower road,
were for this reason both captured.
B3.9.5 Bào Shū led an army and came to speak, saying:
“Prince Jiū
is a kinsman;
we request that you, the ruler, execute him.
Guǎn and Shào are enemies;
we request to receive them to satisfy our hearts.”
Thereupon Prince Jiū was killed at Shēng Dòu.
Shào Hū died for him.
Guǎn Zhòng requested to be imprisoned,
Bào Shū received him,
and upon reaching Táng Fù, he released him.
Returning, he reported this, saying:
“Guǎn Yí Wú is better at governing than Gāo Xī;
it would be well to make him prime minister.”
The Duke followed this.
A3.10 The Annals of Duke Zhuāng, Tenth Year
A3.10.1 In the spring of the tenth year,
in the first month of the King’s calendar,
the Duke defeated the Qí army at Cháng Sháo.
A3.10.2 In the second month,
the Duke invaded Sòng.
A3.10.3 In the third month,
the people of Sòng relocated Sù.
A3.10.4 In summer, in the sixth month,
the Qí army
and the Sòng army halted at Láng.
The Duke defeated the Sòng army at Chéng Qiū.
A3.10.5 In autumn, in the ninth month,
Jīng defeated the Cài army at Shēn,
and returned with the Marquis of Cài, Xiàn Wǔ.
A3.10.6 In winter, in the tenth month,
the Qí army destroyed Tán.
The Viscount of Tán fled to Jǔ.
B3.10 The Commentary of Duke Zhuāng, Tenth Year
B3.10.1 In the spring of the tenth year,
the Qí army attacked us.
The Duke was about to do battle.
Cáo Guì requested an audience.
His fellow villagers said:
“Those who eat meat are planning it;
why should you intervene?”
Guì said:
“Those who eat meat are shallow;
they are unable to plan far ahead.”
He then entered for an audience,
and asked what would be used to fight.
The Duke said:
“Food and clothing, which bring comfort,
I do not dare to keep for myself alone,
but must share them with others.”
He replied:
“Small favors have not reached all;
the people will not follow.”
The Duke said:
“Sacrificial animals, jade, and silks,
I do not dare to increase beyond the truth.
I must be faithful.”
He replied:
“Small faith is not yet fully trustworthy;
the spirits will not grant blessings.”
The Duke said:
“Lawsuits, whether small or great,
even if I cannot investigate all personally,
I must handle according to the facts.”
He replied:
“This is a sign of devotion;
you may fight on this basis.
When you fight,
I request to accompany you.”
The Duke shared his chariot with him.
They fought at Cháng Sháo.
The Duke was about to sound the drums.
Guì said:
“Not yet.”
The Qí people drummed three times.
Guì said:
“Now!”
The Qí army was soundly defeated.
The Duke was about to gallop after them.
Guì said:
“Not yet.”
He got down,
inspected their wheel tracks,
then mounted the carriage bar and looked afar at them,
saying:
“Now!”
They then pursued the Qí army.
After the victory,
the Duke asked for the reason.
He replied:
“In battle, it is a matter of courage.
The first drumming arouses the spirit,
the second causes it to falter,
and the third exhausts it.
Theirs was exhausted while ours was full;
therefore we defeated them.
As for a large state,
it is difficult to fathom,
and I feared an ambush was there.
I saw that their wheel tracks were chaotic
and observed that their flags were trailing;
therefore we pursued them.”
B3.10.2 In summer, in the sixth month,
the Qí and Sòng armies halted at Láng.
Prince Yǎn said:
“The Sòng army is not in order;
it can be defeated.
If Sòng is defeated,
Qí will surely return.
I request to attack them.”
The Duke did not grant it.
He secretly went out from the Yú Gate,
covered his horses with tiger skins, and was the first to attack them.
The Duke followed him
and greatly defeated the Sòng army at Shèngqiū.
The Qí army then returned.
B3.10.3 Marquess Āi of Cài married a lady from Chén;
the Marquis of Xī also married there.
As Xī Guī was going to her husband's home,
she passed through Cài.
The Marquis of Cài said,
"She is my wife's sister."
He stopped her to see her,
but did not treat her with the courtesy due to a guest.
When the Marquis of Xī heard of this,
he was angry
and sent a message to King Wén of Chǔ, saying,
"Attack me;
I will then seek rescue from Cài, and you can attack them."
The Viscount of Chǔ followed this plan.
In the autumn, the ninth month,
Chǔ defeated the Cài army at Shēn
and took the Marquis of Cài, Xiànwǔ, back as a captive.
B3.10.4 When the Marquis of Qí fled his state,
he passed through Tán,
and Tán did not treat him with ritual propriety.
When he returned to his state,
the feudal lords all sent congratulations,
but Tán again did not arrive.
In winter,
the Qí army annihilated Tán
because Tán had been without ritual propriety.
The Viscount of Tán fled to Jǔ,
because they were allies.
A3.11 *The Classic of the Eleventh Year of Duke Zhuāng*
A3.11.1 In the spring of the eleventh year,
the King's first month.
A3.11.2 In the summer, the fifth month,
on the day wùyín,
the Duke defeated the Sòng army at Zī.
A3.11.3 In the autumn,
there was a great flood in Sòng.
A3.11.4 In the winter,
the King's daughter went to her husband's home in Qí.
B3.11 *The Commentary for the Eleventh Year of Duke Zhuāng*
B3.11.1 In the summer of the eleventh year,
because of the battle of Shèngqiū,
Sòng invaded us.
The Duke resisted them.
He pressed the Sòng army before they had formed their ranks
and defeated them at Zī.
In all matters of the army,
if the enemy has not yet formed ranks, it is called
"defeating such-and-such army";
if both have formed ranks, it is called "battled";
if there is a total rout, it is called "utterly defeated."
If victory is achieved through excellence, it is called "conquered";
if the enemy is ambushed and defeated, it is called "captured such-and-such army";
if the Royal Capital's army is defeated, it is called
"the King's army was utterly defeated at such-and-such place."
B3.11.2 In the autumn,
there was a great flood in Sòng.
The Duke sent an envoy to express condolences,
saying,
"Heaven has produced excessive rain,
damaging the sacrificial grains;
how could I not express my condolences?"
The reply said,
"I [the Orphan] was indeed irreverent,
and Heaven sent down this disaster;
this has also become a worry for you, my lord,
and I bow in response to the favor of your message."
Zāng Wénzhòng said,
"Sòng will surely rise!
Yǔ and Tāng took the blame upon themselves,
and their rise was vigorous.
Jié and Zhòu blamed others,
and their fall was sudden.
Furthermore, when a state has a disaster,
for its ruler to call himself 'the Orphan'
is ritual propriety.
His words show trepidation and his self-appellation is ritual;
he is nearly there!"
Later it was heard,
"These were the words of Gōngzǐ Yùyuè."
Zāngsūn Dá said,
"This man is suitable to be a ruler,
as he has a heart that pities the people."
B3.11.3 In the winter,
the Marquis of Qí came to meet Gòng Jī.
B3.11.4 At the battle of Shèngqiū,
the Duke shot Nángōng Chángwàn with the Jīnpúgū arrow,
and the Duke's right-hand attendant Chuán Sūn captured him alive.
The people of Sòng requested his return.
The Duke of Sòng mocked him,
saying,
"At first I respected you;
now you
are a prisoner of Lǔ,
and I no longer respect you."
This humiliated him.
A3.12 *The Classic of the Twelfth Year of Duke Zhuāng*
A3.12.1 In the spring of the twelfth year,
the King's third month,
Shū Jī of Jǐ went to Xī.
A3.12.2 In the summer, the fourth month.
A3.12.3 In the autumn, the eighth month, on the day jiǎwǔ,
Sòng Wàn assassinated his ruler Jié and his grand master Qiú Mù.
A3.12.4 In the winter, the tenth month,
Sòng Wàn fled to Chén.
B3.12 *The Commentary for the Twelfth Year of Duke Zhuāng*
B3.12.1 In the autumn of the twelfth year,
Sòng Wàn assassinated Duke Mǐn at Méngzé.
He encountered Qiú Mù at the gate
and killed him with a blow of his hand.
He encountered Grand Steward Dū to the west of the East Palace
and killed him as well.
He installed Zǐyóu.
The various princes fled to Xiāo,
and Gōngzǐ Yùyuè fled to Bó;
Nángōng Niú and
Měng Huò led an army to besiege Bó.
In the winter, the tenth month,
Xiāo Shú Dàxīn and the clans of Dài, Wǔ, Xuān, Mù, and Zhuāng
attacked them with the army of Cáo.
They killed Nángōng Niú in the army
and killed Zǐyóu in Sòng,
then installed Duke Huán.
Měng Huò fled to Wèi.
Nángōng Wàn fled to Chén,
pulling his mother in a carriage,
arriving in a single day.
The people of Sòng requested Měng Huò from Wèi.
The people of Wèi did not want to give him up.
Shí Qízǐ said,
"It is not permissible.
Wickedness under heaven is the same everywhere;
if he is wicked toward Sòng and we protect him,
what is the benefit of protecting him?
To gain one man and lose a whole state,
to side with evil and abandon friendship,
is not a sound strategy."
The people of Wèi returned him.
They also requested Nángōng Wàn from Chén
with bribes.
The people of Chén had women make him drink wine
and wrapped him in rhinoceros skin.
By the time they reached Sòng,
his hands and feet had broken through.
The people of Sòng minced them both into meat paste.
A3.13 *The Classic of the Thirteenth Year of Duke Zhuāng*
A3.13.1 In the spring of the thirteenth year,
the Marquis of Qí,
men of Sòng,
men of Chén,
men of Cài,
and men of Zhū met at Běixìng.
A3.13.2 In the summer, the sixth month,
the people of Qí annihilated Suì.
A3.13.3 Autumn, the seventh month.
A3.13.4 In the winter,
the Duke met the Marquis of Qí and made a covenant at Kē.
B3.13 *The Commentary for the Thirteenth Year of Duke Zhuāng*
B3.13.1 In the spring of the thirteenth year,
they met at Běixìng
to settle the turmoil in Sòng.
The people of Suì did not arrive.
In the summer,
the people of Qí annihilated Suì and stationed troops there.
B3.13.2 In the winter,
they made a covenant at Kē;
this was the beginning of peace with Qí.
B3.13.3 The people of Sòng turned their backs on the meeting at Běixìng.
A3.14 *The Classic of the Fourteenth Year of Duke Zhuāng*
A3.14.1 In the spring of the fourteenth year,
the people of Qí,
the people of Chén,
and the people of Cáo attacked Sòng.
A3.14.2 In summer,
Shàn Bó met with the others to attack Sòng.
A3.14.3 In autumn, in the seventh month,
Jīng entered Cài.
A3.14.4 In winter,
Shàn Bó met the Marquis of Qí,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Wèi,
and the Earl of Zhèng at Juàn.
B3.14 Commentary on the Fourteenth Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.14.1 In the spring of the fourteenth year,
the feudal lords attacked Sòng.
Qí requested troops from Zhōu.
In summer,
Shàn Bó met them.
They made peace with Sòng and returned.
B3.14.2 Earl Lì of Zhèng invaded Zhèng from Lì;
reaching Dàlíng,
he captured Fù Xiá.
Fù Xiá said:
"If you spare me,
I pray to restore you, my lord."
The Earl made a covenant with him and released him.
In the sixth month, on the day jiǎzǐ,
Fù Xiá killed Zhèng Zǐ and his two sons,
and restored Earl Lì.
Previously,
an inner snake and an outer snake fought within the south gate of Zhèng;
the inner snake died.
Six years later, Earl Lì entered.
The Duke heard of this
and asked Shēn Xū:
"Are there really such portents?"
He replied:
"When people have things they dread,
their own vital energy brings them about.
Portents arise from people.
If people have no flaws,
portents do not arise of themselves.
When people abandon the constants of conduct,
then portents arise;
thus there are portents."
Earl Lì entered
and then killed Fù Xiá.
He sent someone to say to Yuán Fán:
"Fù Xiá was double-minded;
Zhōu has constant punishments,
and he has already submitted to his crime.
To those who restored me without double-mindedness,
I have promised the affairs of High Grand Master;
I wish to plan things with you, Uncle.
Furthermore, when I went out into exile,
you, Uncle, offered no word from within.
When I entered,
you again did not think of me;
I am resentful of this."
He replied:
"The former ruler, Duke Huán, commanded my ancestors to take charge of the ancestral shrine.
When the altars of the soil and grain have a master,
if one turns his heart outward,
what disloyalty could be greater?
As long as one is the master of the altars,
among the people within the state,
who would not be his subject?
That a subject has no double-mindedness
is the regulation of Heaven.
Zǐ Yí has been on the throne
for fourteen years;
as for those who plotted to summon you, my lord,
is that not double-mindedness?
Duke Zhuāng has eight sons remaining;
if all of them used offices and ranks to offer bribes and encourage disloyalty
so as to succeed in their affairs,
what would you do about it, my lord?
I have heard your command."
He then hanged himself and died.
B3.14.3 Because of the incident at Shēn, Marquis Āi of Cài
praised the beauty of Xī Guī to the Viscount of Chǔ.
The Viscount of Chǔ went to Xī,
entered for a feast on the pretext of an offering,
and then extinguished Xī.
He returned with Xī Guī,
who gave birth to Dǔ Áo and King Chéng there.
She did not speak.
The Viscount of Chǔ asked her about it.
She replied:
"I am but one woman,
yet I have served two husbands;
even if I cannot die,
what is there left to say?"
The Viscount of Chǔ, because the Marquis of Cài had caused the destruction of Xī,
then attacked Cài.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
Chǔ entered Cài.
The noble man said:
"What the *Book of Shāng* calls
'The ease with which evil spreads
is like a fire blazing on the plain:
it cannot be approached,
yet it might still be extinguished'
does this not refer to Marquis Āi of Cài!"
B3.14.4 In winter,
they met at Juàn,
because Sòng had submitted.
A3.15 Classic of the Fifteenth Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.15.1 In the spring of the fifteenth year,
the Marquis of Qí,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Chén,
the Marquis of Wèi,
and the Earl of Zhèng met at Juàn.
A3.15.2 In summer,
the Lady Jiāng went to Qí.
A3.15.3 In autumn,
the people of Sòng,
the people of Qí,
and the people of Zhū attacked Ní.
A3.15.4 The people of Zhèng invaded Sòng.
A3.15.5 In the tenth month of winter.
B3.15 Commentary on the Fifteenth Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.15.1 In the spring of the fifteenth year,
they met there again;
Qí began to exercise hegemony.
B3.15.2 In autumn,
the feudal lords attacked Ní on behalf of Sòng.
The people of Zhèng took advantage of the opening and invaded Sòng.
A3.16 Classic of the Sixteenth Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.16.1 In the spring of the sixteenth year,
the King's first month.
A3.16.2 In summer,
the people of Sòng,
the people of Qí,
and the people of Wèi attacked Zhèng.
A3.16.3 In autumn,
Jīng attacked Zhèng.
A3.16.4 In the twelfth month of winter,
he met the Marquis of Qí,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Chén,
the Marquis of Wèi,
the Earl of Zhèng,
the Baron of Xǔ,
the Earl of Huá,
and the Viscount of Téng to make a covenant together at Yōu.
A3.16.5 Kè, Viscount of Zhū, died.
B3.16 Commentary on the Sixteenth Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.16.1 In the summer of the sixteenth year,
the feudal lords attacked Zhèng
because of Sòng.
B3.16.2 The Earl of Zhèng entered from Lì
but was slow to inform Chǔ.
In autumn,
Chǔ attacked Zhèng
and reached Lì,
because of the lack of courtesy.
B3.16.3 The Earl of Zhèng dealt with those who had participated in the rebellion of Yōng Jiū;
in the ninth month,
he killed Young Lord È
and cut off the feet of Qiáng Chú.
Gōngfù Dìngshū fled to Wèi.
Three years later he was restored,
the Earl saying:
"Gòngshū must not be left without descendants in Zhèng."
He was made to enter in the tenth month,
the Earl saying:
"It is a good month;
it reaches a full number."
The noble man said that Qiáng Chú
was unable to protect his own feet.
B3.16.4 In winter,
they made a covenant together at Yōu,
for Zhèng had made peace.
B3.16.5 The King sent the Duke of Guó to charge the Earl of Qūwò
with the command of one army as the Marquis of Jìn.
B3.16.6 Previously,
Jìn Wǔ Gōng attacked Yí,
and captured Yí Guǐzhū.
Wěi Guó requested and secured his release.
Afterward, he did not show gratitude,
so Zǐ Guó started a rebellion,
telling the people of Jìn:
"Join me in attacking Yí and take its land."
He then led the Jìn army to attack Yí,
and killed Yí Guǐzhū.
Zhōu Gōng Jìfù fled to Guó.
When Huì Wáng was established, he restored him.
A3.17 The Classic of the 17th Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.17.1 In the seventeenth year, in spring,
the people of Qí seized Zhèng Zhān.
A3.17.2 In summer,
the people of Qí were annihilated in Suì.
A3.17.3 In autumn,
Zhèng Zhān escaped from Qí and came here.
A3.17.4 In winter,
there were many elks.
B3.17 The Commentary on the 17th Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.17.1 In the spring of the seventeenth year,
the people of Qí seized Zhèng Zhān,
because Zhèng did not attend court.
B3.17.2 In summer,
the Yīn clan of Suì,
the Hé clan,
the Gōnglóu clan,
and the Xūsuì clan feasted the Qí garrison,
got them drunk and killed them,
and thus the people of Qí were annihilated there.
A3.18 The Classic of the 18th Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.18.1 In the eighteenth year, in spring,
in the royal third month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
A3.18.2 In summer,
the Duke pursued the Róng to the west of the Jì River.
A3.18.3 In autumn,
there were *yù*.
A3.18.4 In winter, the tenth month.
B3.18 The Commentary on the 18th Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.18.1 In the spring of the eighteenth year,
the Duke of Guó
and the Marquis of Jìn went to court to see the King.
The King hosted a feast with sweet wine
and ordered them to drink.
To each he granted five pairs of jade
and four horses,
which was not in accordance with ritual.
When the King gives orders to the feudal lords,
as their names and ranks are not the same,
the ritual numbers also differ;
one does not use ritual to grant personal favors to others.
B3.18.2 The Duke of Guó, the Marquis of Jìn, and the Earl of Zhèng
sent Yuán Zhuāng Gōng to welcome the King's bride from Chén.
Guī of Chén returned to the capital;
she was actually Queen Huì.
B3.18.3 In summer,
the Duke pursued the Róng to the west of the Jì River.
That the text does not say they came
is to conceal the matter.
B3.18.4 In autumn,
there were *yù*,
which were a disaster.
B3.18.5 Previously,
Chǔ Wǔ Wáng conquered Quán
and made Dòu Mín its governor;
he rebelled,
and they besieged and killed him.
They moved Quán to Nàchù
and made Yán Áo its governor.
When Wén Wáng took the throne,
he joined with the Bā people to attack Shēn,
and startled their army.
The Bā people rebelled against Chǔ and attacked Nàchù,
captured it,
and then reached the gates of Chǔ.
Yán Áo swam the Yǒng River and escaped.
The Viscount of Chǔ killed him.
His clan started a rebellion.
In winter,
the Bā people took advantage of this to attack Chǔ.
A3.19 The Classic of the 19th Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.19.1 In the nineteenth year, in spring,
in the royal first month.
A3.19.2 In summer, the fourth month.
A3.19.3 In autumn,
Gōngzǐ Jié escorted a bride for a man of Chén to Juàn,
and subsequently made a covenant with the Marquis of Qí
and the Duke of Sòng.
A3.19.4 The Lady Jiāng Shì went to Jǔ.
A3.19.5 In winter,
the people of Qí,
Sòng,
and Chén attacked our western border.
B3.19 The Commentary on the 19th Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.19.1 In the spring of the nineteenth year,
the Viscount of Chǔ resisted them,
but was heavily defeated at Jīn.
When he returned,
Yù Quán would not admit him,
so he then attacked Huáng.
He defeated the Huáng army at Jìlíng.
When he returned
and reached Jiǔ,
he fell ill.
In summer, in the sixth month on the day Gēngshēn,
he died.
Yù Quán buried him in the Xīshì.
He also committed suicide
and was buried at Diéhuáng.
Initially,
Yù Quán had strongly remonstrated with the Viscount of Chǔ.
The Viscount of Chǔ did not follow his advice.
He threatened him with a weapon,
and the Viscount fearfully followed it.
Yù Quán said:
"I frightened my lord with a weapon;
no crime is greater than this."
He then cut off his own feet.
The people of Chǔ made him the Grand Gatekeeper
and called him Dàbó.
They let his descendants hold the office.
The gentleman says:
"Yù Quán can be said to have loved his lord:
he remonstrated and thus brought punishment upon himself,
yet even while punished, he did not forget to lead his lord to goodness."
B3.19.2 Initially,
Wáng Yáo was a favorite of Zhuāng Wáng,
and gave birth to Zǐ Tuí.
Zǐ Tuí was favored,
and Wěi Guó was his tutor.
When Huì Wáng took the throne,
he took Wěi Guó's garden to make it a park.
Biān Bó's palace was close to the King's palace,
and the King took it.
The King seized the fields of Zǐ Qín Zhùguì and Zhān Fù,
and revoked the salary of the royal chef;
therefore Wěi Guó, Biān Bó, Shí Sù, Zhān Fù, and Zǐ Qín Zhùguì rebelled,
relying on the Sū Shì clan.
In autumn,
the five great officials supported Zǐ Tuí to attack the King;
they did not succeed
and fled to Wēn.
Sū Zǐ supported Zǐ Tuí to flee to Wèi.
The armies of Wèi
and Yàn attacked Zhōu.
In winter,
they established Zǐ Tuí.
A3.20 The Classic of the 20th Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.20.1 In the twentieth year, in spring,
in the royal second month,
the Lady Jiāng Shì went to Jǔ.
A3.20.2 In summer,
there was a great disaster in Qí.
A3.20.3 In autumn, the seventh month.
A3.20.4 In winter,
the people of Qí attacked the Róng.
B3.20 The Commentary on the 20th Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.20.1 In the spring of the twentieth year,
the Earl of Zhèng tried to harmonize the Royal House
but did not succeed.
He seized Yàn Zhòngfù.
In summer,
the Earl of Zhèng then returned with the King.
The King stayed at Lì.
In autumn,
the King and the Earl of Zhèng entered Wǔ.
Then they entered Chéngzhōu,
took its treasures, and returned.
In winter,
Prince Tuí feasted the five great officials,
and the music extended to the complete dances.
The Earl of Zhèng heard of this,
and went to see Guó Shū, saying:
"I have heard:
if grief and joy occur at the wrong time,
calamities and disasters will surely arrive.
Now Wángzǐ Tuí sings and dances without tiring,
which is to find joy
in calamity.
Even when the Minister of Justice carries out an execution,
the ruler, for this reason, does not have a full ceremonial meal;
how much more so when one dares to find joy in calamity?
For usurping the King’s position,
what calamity could be greater?
To face calamity and forget one’s worries means
that worries will surely catch up to him.
Why not restore the King?"
Guó Gōng said:
"That is my wish as well."
A3.21 The Annals of the Twenty-First Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.21.1 In the twenty-first year, in spring,
the royal first month.
A3.21.2 In summer, the fifth month, on the day xìnyǒu,
the Earl of Zhèng, Tū, died.
A3.21.3 In autumn, the seventh month, on the day wùxū,
the Lady Jiāng Shì died.
A3.21.4 In winter, the twelfth month,
Duke Lì of Zhèng was buried.
B3.21 The Commentary on the Twenty-First Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.21.1 In the spring of the twenty-first year,
they exchanged commands at Mǐ.
In summer,
they together attacked Wángchéng.
The Earl of Zhèng led the King in through the Yǔmén Gate.
Guó Shū entered through the North Gate.
They killed Wángzǐ Tuí and five high officials.
The Earl of Zhèng feasted the King at the western apartments of the Què,
and the musical performance was complete.
The King gave him the former territory of Duke Wǔ,
from Hǔláo eastward.
Yuán Bó said:
"The Earl of Zhèng is following a bad example;
he too will likely meet with disaster."
In the fifth month,
Duke Lì of Zhèng died.
The King toured the lands of Guó,
and Guó Gōng built a palace for the King at Bàng;
the King gave him Jiǔquán.
When the Earl of Zhèng feasted the King,
the King gave him the Queen's sash-mirror.
Guó Gōng requested ritual vessels,
and the King gave him ritual goblets.
From this time on, the Earl of Zhèng began to feel resentment toward the King.
In winter,
the King returned from Guó.
A3.22 The Annals of the Twenty-Second Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.22.1 In the twenty-second year, in spring,
the royal first month,
a great amnesty was granted.
A3.22.2 On the day guǐchǒu,
we buried our Little Lord, Wén Jiāng.
A3.22.3 The people of Chén killed their Prince Yùkòu.
A3.22.4 In summer, the fifth month.
A3.22.5 In autumn, the seventh month, on the day bǐngshēn,
we made a covenant with Gāo Xī of Qí at Fáng.
A3.22.6 In winter,
the Duke went to Qí to deliver bridal gifts.
B3.22 The Commentary on the Twenty-Second Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.22.1 In the spring of the twenty-second year,
the people of Chén killed their Crown Prince Yùkòu.
Prince Chén Wán and Zhuān Sūn fled to Qí.
Zhuān Sūn came from Qí to flee to our state.
The Marquis of Qí wanted to make Jìng Zhòng a high minister.
He declined, saying:
"A sojourning official like me is lucky to have received pardon
and to benefit from your lenient governance.
That you excuse my lack of training in your instructions
and spare me from criminal punishment,
releasing me from my burdens,
is your lordship's kindness.
What I have received is already much;
how could I dare to disgrace a high position
and thus hasten official slander?
I beg to inform you even unto death.
The Odes say:
'Stately are the chariots and horses,
summoning me with a bow.
Is it that I do not wish to go?
I fear my friends and companions.'"
He was then made Director of Works.
He invited Duke Huán to drink wine,
and they were happy.
The Duke said:
"Continue the feast by torchlight."
He declined, saying:
"Your servant divined for the day,
but I have not divined for the night;
I do not dare."
The superior man says:
"Wine is to complete a ritual,
and not to be followed by excess;
this is righteousness.
To help one's ruler complete a ritual
and not let him fall into excess;
this is benevolence."
Earlier,
the head of the Yì Shì family divined about marrying his daughter to Jìng Zhòng.
His wife interpreted the omen,
saying:
"It is auspicious.
This is called:
'The phoenixes fly together,
singing in harmony with a clanging sound.
The descendants of the Guī
shall be nurtured among the Jiāng.
In five generations they shall flourish,
ranking among the highest ministers.
After eight generations,
none shall be as great as they.'"
Duke Lì of Chén
was born of a woman from Cài;
therefore, the people of Cài killed Wǔfù
and established him.
He sired Jìng Zhòng.
When he was young,
a scribe of Zhōu came to see the Marquis of Chén with the Zhou Yi.
The Marquis of Chén had him perform a divination for the boy.
He encountered the hexagram Guān ䷓ changing into Pǐ
He said:
"This is called
'Observing the glory of the state,
it is advantageous to be a guest of the King.'
Will this person replace Chén and possess the state?
Not here,
but in another state;
not this person himself,
but his descendants.
Glory
is far-reaching and shines from elsewhere.
Kūn
is earth;
Xùn
is wind;
Qián
is heaven.
Wind becoming heaven; above the earth,
that is a mountain.
Having the materials of a mountain
and being illuminated by the light of heaven,
thus he dwells upon the earth.
Therefore it is said:
'Observing the glory of the state,
it is advantageous to be a guest of the King.'
The court offerings are in hundreds,
presented with jade and silk;
the beauties of heaven and earth are all present there.
Therefore it is said:
'it is advantageous to be a guest of the King.'
Yet there is still the word 'observing,'
so I say it will be in the future!
The wind moves and becomes manifest upon the earth,
so I say it will be in another state!
If it is in another state,
it must be one of the Jiāng surname.
The Jiāng
are descendants of Dàyuè.
High mountains match with heaven.
Two things cannot both be great.
When Chén declines,
this one will flourish!"
When Chén first perished,
Chén Huán Zǐ began to be great in Qí;
when it perished later,
Chéng Zǐ gained the government.
A3.23 The Annals of the Twenty-Third Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.23.1 In the twenty-third year, in spring,
the Duke arrived from Qí.
A3.23.2 Zhài Shū came on a mission of state.
A3.23.3 In summer,
the Duke went to Qí to observe the sacrifice to the god of the soil.
A3.23.4 The Duke arrived from Qí.
A3.23.5 The people of Jīng came to pay a courtesy visit.
A3.23.6 The Duke and the Marquis of Qí met at Gǔ.
A3.23.7 Shū of Xiāo had an audience with the Duke.
A3.23.8 In autumn,
the pillars of Huán's temple were painted red.
A3.23.9 In winter, the eleventh month,
Shègū, the Earl of Cáo, died.
A3.23.10 In the twelfth month, on the day jiǎyín,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí and made a covenant at Hù.
B3.23 The Commentary on the Twenty-third Year of Duke Zhuāng.
B3.23.1 In the summer of the twenty-third year,
the Duke went to Qí to observe the sacrifice to the Earth God,
which was a violation of ritual.
Cáo Guì remonstrated, saying:
"This is not permissible.
Ritual
is that which orders the people.
Therefore, meetings are held
to instruct on the principles of high and low
and to establish limits for expenditures;
audiences are held to rectify the duties of rank and nobility
and to follow the order of seniority;
military expeditions are for punishing those who do not comply.
The feudal lords have a King,
and the King has tours of inspection
to practice these matters on a grand scale.
Other than for these purposes,
the ruler does not make a move.
When the ruler moves, it must be recorded;
if it is recorded and is not in accordance with the law,
what will future generations observe?"
B3.23.2 The clans of Huán and Zhuāng in Jìn were pressing,
and Duke Xiàn was troubled by them.
Shì Wěi said:
"Remove Fùzǐ,
then the group of young lords can be dealt with."
The Duke said:
"Try your hand at it."
Shì Wěi plotted with the group of young lords,
slandered Fùzǐ and removed him.
B3.23.3 In autumn,
the pillars of Huán's temple were painted red.
A3.24 The Annals of the Twenty-fourth Year of Duke Zhuāng.
A3.24.1 In the spring of the twenty-fourth year,
in the royal third month,
the rafters of Huán's temple were carved.
A3.24.2 Duke Zhuāng of Cáo was buried.
A3.24.3 In summer,
the Duke went to Qí to meet his bride.
A3.24.4 In autumn,
the Duke arrived from Qí.
A3.24.5 In the eighth month, on the day dīngchǒu,
the Lady Jiāng entered.
A3.24.6 On the day wùyín,
the wives of the high officials had an audience with her,
using gifts of silk.
A3.24.7 There was a great flood.
A3.24.8 In winter,
the Róng invaded Cáo.
A3.24.9 Jī of Cáo fled to Chén.
A3.24.10 Chì returned to Cáo.
A3.24.11 The Duke of Guō.
B3.24 The Commentary on the Twenty-fourth Year of Duke Zhuāng.
B3.24.1 In the spring of the twenty-fourth year,
the carving of the rafters
was a violation of ritual.
Yù Sūn remonstrated, saying:
"I have heard
that frugality
is the commonality of virtue,
and extravagance
is the greatest of evils.
The former ruler possessed the virtue of frugality,
but you, my lord, are leading him into a great evil;
is this not impermissible?"
B3.24.2 In autumn,
Āijiāng arrived.
The Duke had the wives of the high officials have an audience with her,
using gifts of silk,
which was a violation of ritual.
Yù Sūn said:
"For men's ritual gifts,
the greater are jade and silk,
and the lesser are birds and beasts,
to manifest their status.
For women's ritual gifts,
they do not exceed hazelnuts, chestnuts, dates, and dried meat,
to express their reverence.
Now that men and women use the same ritual gifts,
there is no distinction.
The distinction between men and women
is a major regulation of the state;
yet it is being thrown into disorder by the Lady.
Is this not impermissible?"
B3.24.3 Shì Wěi of Jìn again plotted with the group of young lords,
causing them to kill the two sons of the Yóu clan.
Shì Wěi reported to the Marquis of Jìn, saying:
"It is done.
Within no more than two years,
you will certainly have no further trouble."
A3.25 The Annals of the Twenty-fifth Year of Duke Zhuāng.
A3.25.1 In the spring of the twenty-fifth year,
the Marquis of Chén sent Nǚshū to pay a courtesy visit.
A3.25.2 In summer, the fifth month, on the day guǐchǒu,
Shuò, the Marquis of Wèi, died.
A3.25.3 In the sixth month, on the day xīnwèi,
the first day of the month, there was an eclipse of the sun.
Drums were beaten and an animal sacrifice was offered at the altar of the Earth God.
A3.25.4 Bójī went to Kǐ to be married.
A3.25.5 In autumn,
there was a great flood.
Drums were beaten and animal sacrifices were offered at the altar of the Earth God
and at the gates.
A3.25.6 In winter,
Gōngzǐ Yǒu went to Chén.
B3.25 The Commentary on the Twenty-fifth Year of Duke Zhuāng.
B3.25.1 In the spring of the twenty-fifth year,
Nǚshū of Chén came to pay a courtesy visit,
initiating the friendship with Chén.
This was commended,
therefore his name was not recorded.
B3.25.2 In summer, the sixth month, on the day xīnwèi,
the first day of the month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
Drums were beaten and an animal sacrifice was offered at the altar of the Earth God,
which was not according to the norm.
Only on the first day of the first month,
when the evil influences have not yet arisen,
if there is an eclipse of the sun,
then silk is offered at the altar of the Earth God
and drums are beaten at the court.
B3.25.3 In autumn,
there was a great flood.
Drums were beaten and animal sacrifices were offered at the altar of the Earth God
and at the gates,
which also was not according to the norm.
For all natural disasters,
there should be offerings of silk
but no animal sacrifices.
Unless it is an eclipse of the sun or moon, drums are not beaten.
B3.25.4 Shì Wěi of Jìn caused the group of young lords to kill the entire clan of Yóu.
Then a wall was built around Jù for them to reside in.
In winter,
the Marquis of Jìn besieged Jù
and killed all the young lords.
A3.26 The Annals of the Twenty-sixth Year of Duke Zhuāng.
A3.26.1 In the spring of the twenty-sixth year,
the Duke attacked the Róng.
A3.26.2 In summer,
the Duke arrived from attacking the Róng.
A3.26.3 Cáo killed its high official.
A3.26.4 In autumn,
the Duke met with the people of Sòng
and the people of Qí to attack Xú.
A3.26.5 In winter, the twelfth month, on the day guǐhài, the first day of the month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
B3.26 The Commentary on the Twenty-sixth Year of Duke Zhuāng.
B3.26.1 In the spring of the twenty-sixth year,
Shì Wěi of Jìn became the Grand Minister of Works.
B3.26.2 In summer,
Shì Wěi walled Jiàng
to make the palace more secure.
B3.26.3 In autumn,
the people of Guó invaded Jìn.
In winter,
the people of Guó again invaded Jìn.
A3.27 The Annals of the Twenty-seventh Year of Duke Zhuāng.
A3.27.1 In the twenty-seventh year, in spring,
the Duke met Bó Jī of Qǐ at Táo.
A3.27.2 In summer, in the sixth month,
he met with the Marquis of Qí,
the Duke of Sòng,
the Marquis of Chén,
and the Earl of Zhèng,
and they made a covenant together at Yōu.
A3.27.3 In autumn,
Gōngzǐ Yǒu went to Chén
to bury Yuán Zhòng.
A3.27.4 In winter,
Bó Jī of Qǐ came.
A3.27.5 Qìng of Jǔ came to meet Shū Jī.
A3.27.6 The Earl of Qǐ came for an audience.
A3.27.7 The Duke met with the Marquis of Qí at Chéngpú.
B3.27 The Commentary on the Twenty-seventh Year of Duke Zhuāng.
B3.27.1 In the twenty-seventh year, in spring,
the Duke met Bó Jī of Qǐ at Táo,
which was not a proper matter of state.
Unless for a grand display of righteousness, the Son of Heaven does not go on a tour of inspection;
unless for the affairs of the people, a feudal lord does not raise an army;
unless by command of the ruler, a high official does not cross the border.
B3.27.2 In summer,
they made a covenant together at Yōu;
this was because Chén and Zhèng had submitted.
B3.27.3 In autumn,
Gōngzǐ Yǒu went to Chén
to bury Yuán Zhòng,
which was contrary to ritual.
Yuán Zhòng
was an old friend of Jì Yǒu.
B3.27.4 In winter,
Bó Jī of Qǐ came
to inquire after her parents.
Whenever a daughter of a feudal lord
returns to inquire after her parents, it is called "lái" (came);
if she is expelled, it is called "lái guī" (came back).
For a ruler's wife, returning to inquire after parents is called "rú" (goes to) such-and-such;
being expelled is called "guī yú" (returns to) such-and-such.
B3.27.5 The Marquis of Jìn was about to attack Guó.
Shì Wěi said:
"It is not possible.
The Duke of Guó is arrogant.
If he suddenly gains victories over us,
he will surely abandon his people.
After he has no multitude, then attack him.
If he wishes to resist us then,
with whom will he do so?
Now, ritual, music, compassion, and love
are what is accumulated for war.
Only when the people
are yielding in their duties, delight in harmony, love their kin, and mourn for the dead,
can they then be used.
Guó has not accumulated these things.
If they fight frequently,
they will face famine."
B3.27.6 The King sent Zhào Bó Liào to confer a mandate upon the Marquis of Qí
and also requested him to attack Wèi,
because they had established the son Tuí.
A3.28 The Annals of the Twenty-eighth Year of Duke Zhuāng.
A3.28.1 In the twenty-eighth year, in spring,
in the royal third month, on the day jiǎyín,
the people of Qí attacked Wèi.
The people of Wèi and the people of Qí fought;
the people of Wèi were utterly defeated.
A3.28.2 In summer, in the fourth month, on the day dīngwèi,
Suǒ, the Viscount of Zhū, died.
A3.28.3 In autumn,
Jīng attacked Zhèng.
The Duke met with the people of Qí
and the people of Sòng to rescue Zhèng.
A3.28.4 In winter,
they built walls at Méi.
A3.28.5 There was a great failure of wheat
and grain. Zāngsūn Chén reported the purchase of grain from Qí.
B3.28 The Commentary on the Twenty-eighth Year of Duke Zhuāng.
B3.28.1 In the twenty-eighth year, in spring,
the Marquis of Qí attacked Wèi.
They fought
and defeated the army of Wèi.
He rebuked them by the King's command
and returned after taking bribes.
B3.28.2 Duke Xiàn of Jìn took a wife from Jiǎ,
but had no son.
He committed incest with Qí Jiāng,
who gave birth to the wife of Duke Mù of Qín and the Crown Prince Shēn Shēng.
He also took two women from the Róng.
Hú Jī of the Dà Róng gave birth to Chóng'ěr;
Xiǎo Róng Zǐ gave birth to Yí Wú.
Jìn attacked the Lí Róng.
The Lí Róng presented Lí Jī,
who went with him.
She gave birth to Xī Qí,
and her younger sister gave birth to Zhuó Zǐ.
Lí Jī became a favorite
and wished to establish her own son.
She bribed the external favorites Liáng Wǔ and Dōngguān Wǔ
to make them say to the Duke:
"Qǔwò
is your lordship’s ancestral city;
Pú and the two Qū
are your lordship’s borders;
they cannot be without masters.
If the ancestral city has no master,
the people will not be in awe;
if the borders have no masters,
it will open up the hearts of the Róng for invasion.
When the Róng develop such hearts,
and the people neglect their government,
it is a calamity for the state.
If the Crown Prince is made to master Qǔwò,
and Chóng'ěr
and Yí Wú master Pú and Qū,
then the people can be overawed and the Róng made to fear,
and moreover, your lordship’s military achievements will be made manifest."
They were both made to say:
"The vast wilderness of the Dí
would become a capital for Jìn.
For Jìn to open up land,
is it not appropriate?"
The Marquis of Jìn was pleased with this.
In summer,
he sent the Crown Prince to reside in Qǔwò,
Chóng'ěr to reside in the city of Pú,
and Yí Wú to reside in Qū.
All the other sons of the Duke were sent to the border towns.
Only the sons of the two Jī
remained in Jiàng.
The "Two Wǔ" eventually conspired with Lí Jī to slander the sons of the Duke
and establish Xī Qí;
the people of Jìn called them "the pair of two Wǔ."
B3.28.3 Zǐyuán, the Chancellor of Chǔ, wished to seduce Lady Wén.
He built a guest house by the side of her palace
and performed the dance of the "Ten Thousand" there.
When the Lady heard it,
she wept and said:
"The former ruler used this dance
to practice military preparedness.
Now the Chancellor does not seek enemies
but performs it by the side of this widow;
is it not strange?"
An attendant reported this to Zǐyuán.
Zǐyuán said:
"A woman does not forget to attack enemies,
yet I, on the contrary, have forgotten it!"
In autumn,
Zǐyuán led six hundred chariots to attack Zhèng
and entered through the Jié Dié gate.
Zǐyuán, Dòu Yùqiáng, Dòu Wú, and Bǐ of Gěng acted as the vanguard.
Dòu Bān, Wángsūn Yóu, and Wángsūn Xǐ acted as the rearguard.
The mass of chariots entered from the Chún gate
and reached the crossroads of the market.
The hanging gates were not lowered.
They spoke in the Chǔ language and retreated.
Zǐyuán said:
"There are people in Zhèng."
The feudal lords came to the rescue of Zhèng.
The Chǔ army fled by night.
The people of Zhèng were about to flee to Tóngqiū,
but a spy reported:
"There are crows on the tents of Chǔ."
So they stopped.
B3.28.4 In winter,
there was a famine;
Zāngsūn Chén reported the purchase of grain from Qí,
which was in accordance with ritual.
B3.28.5 They built walls at Méi,
which was not a capital.
Regarding cities:
those that have the ancestral temple and the tablets of former rulers
are called "dū" (capitals);
those without are called "yì" (towns).
For a town, it is called "zhù" (building walls);
for a capital, it is called "chéng" (walling).
A3.29 The Annals of the Twenty-ninth Year of Duke Zhuāng.
A3.29.1 In the twenty-ninth year, in spring,
the Yán stables were newly built.
A3.29.2 In summer,
the people of Zhèng invaded Xǔ.
A3.29.3 In autumn,
there were fěi insects.
A3.29.4 In winter, in the twelfth month,
Jì Shūjī died.
Walls were built at Zhū and Fáng.
B3.29 Commentary on the Twenty-ninth Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.29.1 In the twenty-ninth year, in spring,
the Yán stables were newly built;
it was recorded
because it was not the proper time.
Regarding all horses,
they are sent out at the spring equinox
and brought back at the autumn equinox.
B3.29.2 In summer,
the people of Zhèng invaded Xǔ.
For any army,
one with bells and drums is called an attack (fá),
one without them is called an invasion (qīn),
and a swift one is called a raid (xí).
B3.29.3 In autumn,
there were fěi insects,
which were a disaster.
For any thing,
if it does not cause a disaster,
it is not recorded.
B3.29.4 In winter, in the twelfth month,
walls were built at Zhū and Fáng;
it was recorded
because it was the proper time.
For all earthworks,
when the Dragon constellation appears, agricultural tasks are finished,
which serves as a warning for the construction;
when the Fire star appears,
materials are gathered for use;
when the Water star is centered at dusk, the frames are set;
and at the solstice, the work is completed.
B3.29.5 Fán Pí rebelled against the King.
A3.30 Classic of the Thirtieth Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.30.1 In the thirtieth year, in spring,
the first month of the King’s calendar.
A3.30.2 In summer,
the Duke halted at Chéng.
A3.30.3 In autumn, in the seventh month,
the people of Qí brought about the surrender of Zhāng.
In the eighth month, on the day guǐhài,
Jì Shūjī was buried.
A3.30.5 In the ninth month, on the day gēngwǔ, the first day of the month,
there was an eclipse of the sun;
drums were beaten and animals were sacrificed at the altar of the earth.
A3.30.6 In winter,
the Duke and the Marquis of Qí met at Lǔjì.
The people of Qí attacked the Shānróng.
B3.30 Commentary on the Thirtieth Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.30.1 In the thirtieth year, in spring,
the King ordered the Duke of Guó to punish Fán Pí.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day bǐngchén,
the Duke of Guó entered Fán,
captured Fán Zhòngpí,
and sent him back to the capital Jīngshī.
B3.30.2 Prince Yuán of Chǔ returned from attacking Zhèng
and resided in the King's palace;
Dòu Shèshī remonstrated,
but was seized and put in stocks.
In autumn,
Dòu Bān, the Governor of Shēn, killed Zǐyuán.
Dòu Gǔyútù became the Lìngyǐn;
he depleted his own family's resources
to relieve the difficulties of the state of Chǔ.
B3.30.3 In winter,
they met at Lǔjì
to plan against the Shānróng
because they were distressing Yān.
A3.31 Classic of the Thirty-first Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.31.1 In the thirty-first year, in spring,
a terrace was built at Láng.
A3.31.2 In summer, in the fourth month,
the Earl of Xuē died.
A3.31.3 A terrace was built at Xuē.
In the sixth month,
the Marquis of Qí came to present the spoils of the Róng.
A3.31.5 In autumn,
a terrace was built at Qín.
A3.31.6 In winter,
it did not rain.
B3.31 Commentary on the Thirty-first Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.31.1 In the thirty-first year, in summer, in the sixth month,
the Marquis of Qí came to present the spoils of the Róng,
which was contrary to ritual.
Generally, when a feudal lord achieves success against the four non-Chinese peoples,
he presents it to the King,
so that the King may use it to warn the non-Chinese peoples;
against the central states, he does not.
Feudal lords do not send captives to one another.
A3.32 Classic of the Thirty-second Year of Duke Zhuāng
A3.32.1 In the thirty-second year, in spring,
walls were built at Xiǎogǔ.
A3.32.2 In summer,
the Duke of Sòng and
the Marquis of Qí met at Liángqiū.
A3.32.3 In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day guǐsì,
Gōngzǐ Yá died.
A3.32.4 In the eighth month, on the day guǐhài,
the Duke passed away in the main bedchamber.
A3.32.5 In winter, in the tenth month, on the day jǐwèi,
Zǐbān died.
A3.32.6 Gōngzǐ Qìngfù went to Qí.
A3.32.7 The Dí attacked Xíng.
B3.32 Commentary on the Thirty-second Year of Duke Zhuāng
B3.32.1 In the thirty-second year, in spring,
walls were built at Xiǎogǔ
for the sake of Guǎn Zhòng.
B3.32.2 Because Chǔ had attacked Zhèng, the Marquis of Qí
requested a meeting with the feudal lords.
The Duke of Sòng requested to see the Marquis of Qí first.
In summer,
they met at Liángqiū.
B3.32.3 In autumn, in the seventh month,
a spirit descended at Shēn.
King Huì asked Nèishǐ Guò,
"What is the reason for this?"
He replied,
"When a state is about to rise,
an enlightened spirit descends upon it
to observe its virtue;
when it is about to perish,
a spirit also descends
to observe its wickedness.
Thus some have obtained a spirit and risen,
and some have also because of it perished.
Yú, Xià,
Shāng, and Zhōu all had such instances."
The King said,
"What should be done?"
He replied,
"Make offerings to it with its appropriate things.
The day of its arrival
also determines the nature of the offerings."
The King followed this.
Nèishǐ Guò went there and
heard that Guó was requesting a mandate;
upon returning, he said,
"Guó will surely perish.
They are oppressive yet listen to spirits."
The spirit stayed at Shēn for six months.
The Duke of Guó sent Zhù Yìng, Zōng Qū, and Shǐ Yín to make offerings to it.
The spirit granted them land.
Shǐ Yín said,
"Guó will perish!
I have heard:
when a state is about to rise,
it listens to the people;
when it is about to perish,
it listens to spirits.
Spirits
are intelligent, upright, and impartial,
and they act in accordance with people.
Guó is deficient in virtue;
how can they obtain any land?"
B3.32.4 Previously,
the Duke built a terrace
overlooking the house of the Dǎng clan;
he saw Mèng Rèn
and followed her.
She shut the door.
And because of the Lady's words
he promised her,
cutting his arm to swear a covenant with her,
and Zǐ Bān was born of her.
At the sacrifice for rain,
a rehearsal was held at the house of the Liáng clan,
and the young lady went to watch it.
The groom Luò, from outside the wall,
teased her.
Zǐ Bān was angry
and had him whipped.
The Duke said:
"It would be better to kill him;
this is not a man to be whipped.
Luò is strong;
he can throw a canopy over the Jì Gate."
The Duke fell ill
and asked Shū Yá about the succession.
He replied:
"Qìng Fù has talent."
He asked Jì Yǒu.
He replied:
"Your servant will serve Zǐ Bān even unto death."
The Duke said:
"Earlier, Yá said,
'Qìng Fù has talent.'"
Chéng Jì, using the Ruler's command,
ordered Xī Shú to wait at the house of the Zhēn Wū clan,
and sent Zhēn Jì to poison him with wine.
He said:
"Drink this,
and you shall have descendants in the state of Lǔ;
if not,
you will die and have no descendants."
He drank it,
returned home,
and reached Kuí Quán where he died.
The Shū Sūn clan was established.
B3.32.5 In the eighth month, on guǐhài,
the Duke died in the principal chamber.
Zǐ Bān ascended the throne
and stayed at the house of the Dǎng clan.
In winter, the tenth month, on jǐwèi,
Gòng Zhòng
sent the groom Luò
to assassinate Zǐ Bān at the house of the Dǎng clan.
Chéng Jì fled to Chén. Duke Mǐn was established.
A4.1 The Classic of the First Year of Duke Mǐn.
A4.1.1 In the spring of the first year,
the Royal first month.
A4.1.2 The people of Qí rescued Xíng.
A4.1.3 In the summer, the sixth month, on xīnyǒu,
we buried our ruler, Duke Zhuāng.
A4.1.4 In the autumn, the eighth month,
the Duke and the Marquis of Qí made a covenant at Luògū.
Jì Zǐ came back.
A4.1.5 In the winter,
Zhòngsūn of Qí came.
B4.1 The Commentary on the First Year of Duke Mǐn.
B4.1.1 In the spring of the first year,
his accession is not recorded
because of the disorder.
B4.1.2 The Dí people attacked Xíng.
Guǎn Jìng Zhòng said to the Marquis of Qí:
"The Róng and the Dí are like jackals and wolves,
they can never be satisfied;
the various states of Xià are close kin,
they must not be abandoned.
Seeking ease and comfort is like drinking poisoned wine,
it should not be cherished.
The Shī says:
'How could I not cherish the thought of returning?
But I fear this brief letter.'
'Brief letter'
refers to mutual sympathy in common distress.
I request that we rescue Xíng
to follow the brief letter."
The people of Qí rescued Xíng.
B4.1.3 In the summer, the sixth month,
Duke Zhuāng was buried.
Because of the disorder,
it was thus delayed.
B4.1.4 In the autumn, the eighth month,
the Duke and the Marquis of Qí made a covenant at Luògū,
requesting the return of Jì Yǒu.
The Marquis of Qí granted it,
and sent for him from Chén,
while the Duke stayed at Láng to wait for him.
"Jì Zǐ came back"
is used to praise him.
B4.1.5 In the winter,
Zhòngsūn Qiū of Qí came to investigate the troubles.
The record says
"Zhòngsūn,"
also to praise him.
When Zhòngsūn returned,
he said:
"If Qìng Fù is not removed,
the troubles in Lǔ will not end."
The Duke said:
"How shall we remove him?"
He replied:
"If the troubles do not end,
he will bring about his own destruction;
your Lordship should wait for it."
The Duke asked:
"Can Lǔ be taken?"
He replied:
"No.
They still uphold the Zhōu Lǐ.
The Zhōu Lǐ
is the root.
I have heard it said:
'When a state is about to perish,
its roots must first fall,
and then the branches and leaves follow.'
Since Lǔ does not abandon the Zhōu Lǐ,
it cannot yet be moved.
Your Lordship should strive to settle the troubles of Lǔ
and befriend them.
To befriend those who possess ritual,
to rely on those who are steady and firm,
to separate those who are wavering,
and to overthrow those who are in dark disorder
are the instruments of a Hegemon or King."
B4.1.6 The Marquis of Jìn created two armies;
the Duke commanded the Upper Army,
and the Crown Prince Shēn Shēng commanded the Lower Army.
Zhào Sù drove the Duke's chariot,
and Bì Wàn was the spearman on the right,
with which they destroyed Gěng, destroyed Huò, and destroyed Wèi.
On their return,
they walled Qǔ Wò for the Crown Prince,
granted Gěng to Zhào Sù,
and granted Wèi to Bì Wàn,
making them high officers.
Shì Wěi said:
"The Crown Prince will not be established.
He was given a capital city
and a rank of high minister;
having reached the ultimate position prematurely,
how can he be established?
It would be better for him to flee,
so as not to let guilt reach him.
To become like Wú Tài Bó,
would that not be acceptable?
He would still have a good name,
rather than waiting for disaster.
Moreover, a proverb says:
'If the heart is without flaw,
why worry about having no home?'
If Heaven favors the Crown Prince,
will it not be outside Jìn?"
Bǔ Yǎn said:
"The descendants of Bì Wàn will surely be great.
'Wàn'
is a full number;
'Wèi'
is a great name.
Since the rewards began with these,
Heaven has opened the way for them.
The Son of Heaven speaks of the million people,
and the feudal lords speak of the ten thousand people.
Now that his name is 'Great'
and it follows a full number,
he will surely have the masses."
Earlier,
when Bì Wàn first divined about taking office in Jìn,
he encountered the hexagram Zhūn changing to Bǐ.
Xīn Liào interpreted it,
saying:
"Auspicious.
Zhūn is firmness; Bǐ is entry.
What could be more auspicious than this?
He will surely prosper and multiply.
Zhèn becomes the earth,
the chariot follows the horse,
the feet dwell in it,
the elder brother leads it,
the mother protects it,
